newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand seeks to slash costs.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand seeks to slash costs.

text.p: - Storebrand ASA chief executive officer Age Korsvold has called on staff to propose ways of cutting costs by 40 percent in each unit of Norway's largest insurance group, although not all of the proposals may be implemented.
"It is not an aim in itself to do things differently but we know that, over time, routines get established that are not really necessary," he wrote in the in-house magazine Vi (We) this week.
"It is also clear that we face an important challenge in avoiding double work in our nine business areas in addition to in strategic staffs and joint services," Korsvold said.
The company announced a cost-cut campaign in August.

"We have established a minimum framework for proposed cost cuts amounting to 40 percent per unit. The reason is that we want to think in new ways and leave no stone unturned in the initial phase. The steering committee will prioritise measures within this framework that are deemed feasible."

In August, Korsvold presented the company's first half operating profit of 2.76 billion crowns before the distribution to life policy-holders, 766 million crowns higher than in the January-June period 1995.

He said then that competition in the Norwegian insurance industry called for better cost effectiveness throughout the group, and the effect of the accounts would be recorded in the third quarter 1996.
"What's important is that we make fundamental changes in the way we sell and distribute our products," he said.
